title: A morphism of etale sheaves is an isomorphism iff it is one on an etale covering
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(t_i:T_i\to T)_{i\in I}$ be a family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] which is jointly surjective (every point of $T$ lies in the image of some $t_i$). Let $\varphi:G\to H$ be a morphism in the category $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if for every $i$ its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] $t_i^{-1}\varphi:t_i^{-1}G\to t_i^{-1}H$ is an isomorphism in $\Ab(T_{i,\Et})$. (For $I=\emptyset$, $T$ is empty and every morphism of $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is an isomorphism.)

source.place: proof of Etale Cohomology, Lemma label lemma-base-change-local, Tag 0EZR, last sentence of the proof of (1) ("we conclude it is an isomorphism as $\{U_i\to X\}$ is an etale covering"); with Theorem label theorem-exactness-stalks, Tag 03PU (geometric stalks detect isomorphisms) and Lemma label lemma-stalk-pullback, Tag 03Q1 ($(f^{-1}G)_{\bar s}=G_{f(\bar s)}$). Route intended by the item that created this node: geometric stalks are conservative (node lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative, Lean closed); every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ over $t$ lifts to some $T_i$ (choose $s\in T_i$ over $t$; $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(s)$ is finite separable, so it embeds into the algebraically closed field of $\bar t$ over $\kappa(t)$); and $(t_i^{-1}G)_{\bar s}\cong G_{\bar t}$ for a lift $\bar s$, naturally in $G$.

proof.text: *The easy direction.* If $\varphi$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\psi$, then $t_i^{-1}$, being a functor $\Ab(T_{\Et})\to\Ab(T_{i,\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], sends $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$ and $\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_H$ to $t_i^{-1}\psi\circ t_i^{-1}\varphi=\mathrm{id}$ and $t_i^{-1}\varphi\circ t_i^{-1}\psi=\mathrm{id}$; so every $t_i^{-1}\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: proof of Lemma label lemma-base-change-local, Tag 0EZR (functoriality of restriction, implicit)

proof.text: *Lifting a geometric point.* Assume every $t_i^{-1}\varphi$ is an isomorphism, and let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be any geometric point of $T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], lying over $t\in T$. Since the etale family $(t_i)$ is jointly surjective there are $i\in I$ and $s\in T_i$ with $t_i(s)=t$, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] gives a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_i$ over $s$ with $t_i\circ\bar s=\bar t$. (If $I=\emptyset$ then $T=\emptyset$, there is no geometric point, and this step and the next are vacuous.)

source.place: Lemma label lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover, Tag 03PR, with $(U,\bar u)=(T,\bar t)$ and the covering $\{T_i\to T\}$

proof.text: *The stalk of the pullback is the stalk at the image.* For the geometric point $\bar s$ of $T_i$ of step 2 there is an isomorphism $c_K:(t_i^{-1}K)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{t_i\circ\bar s}=K_{\bar t}$ of stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], natural in the abelian sheaf $K$ on $T_{\Et}$ [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] (its $f^*$ is the inverse image $f^{-1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]: in the Lean, `Etale.upperStar` is the sheaf pullback along the base-change functor $T_{\Et}\to T_{i,\Et}$, i.e. the sheafified presheaf inverse image; Stacks 03Q1 (3) is the same identification). Naturality in $K$ applied to $\varphi:G\to H$ gives $\varphi_{\bar t}\circ c_G=c_H\circ(t_i^{-1}\varphi)_{\bar s}$. The stalk at $\bar s$ is a functor (a colimit of sections), so it sends the isomorphism $t_i^{-1}\varphi$ to an isomorphism $(t_i^{-1}\varphi)_{\bar s}$; hence $\varphi_{\bar t}=c_H\circ(t_i^{-1}\varphi)_{\bar s}\circ c_G^{-1}$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups.

source.place: Lemma label lemma-stalk-pullback, Tag 03Q1 (3): $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_{\bar x}=\mathcal G_{f\circ\bar x}$

proof.text: *Geometric stalks detect isomorphisms.* By steps 2 and 3, $\varphi_{\bar t}:G_{\bar t}\to H_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$. A morphism of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ that is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk is an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; so $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. (In the Lean, `Scheme.isIso_of_isIso_sheafFiber_map` asks this only at one universe-lifted geometric point over each point of $T$, which is among the geometric points just treated.) This proves the converse direction.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks 0EZR (1), 03PU, 03Q1). Proof written in four steps along the stalk route named in the source field: the forward direction by functoriality of t_i^{-1} (elementary); the converse by lifting each geometric point of T to some T_i (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift = Stacks 03PR, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_fac_of_etale_of_isSepClosed), identifying the stalk of t_i^{-1}phi at the lift with the stalk of phi (lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar, Lean closed, Stacks 03Q1 (3)), and concluding with the conservativity of geometric stalks (lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative, Lean closed, Stacks 03PU). The two closed lemmas are tools (units sk-thm-p1 and sk-prop-cd). The mono-only leaf lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono does not fit (it would need a separate epi half) and is not used. Mathlib's Sheaf.isIso_iff_of_coversTop was read: it is a generalization, missing the CoversTop of the family, the site equivalence (T_et)/T_i = T_{i,et}, and the identification of overPullback (plain restriction) with the inverse image (lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction); recorded in mathlib_searches. No Lean exists for the item.
